title: The Shallows Where Copper Bleeds

features.name: corroded overflow
features.desc-on-touch: the pipe weeps oxidized copper into the shallows; its voice is three-fold, turning in the current

features.name: settling pool
features.desc-on-touch: you wade in tinted water; the discolouration arranges itself into settled strata

features.name: testing station marker
features.desc-on-touch: a faded enamel sign announces water quality sampling; the dates have run together

features.name: upstream debris field
features.desc-on-touch: broken copper fittings and old pipe segments lie in the shallows, arranged by current into a language you almost read

features.name: echo chamber
features.desc-on-touch: water moving through rusted piping makes a sound like singing; three voices in different keys, none of them human

inscription: the copper has bled long enough that the water learned its taste; now the water teaches the copper what colour to become

file.name: CouncilLetter_Re_WaterDiscolouration_1987.txt
file.note: official complaint turns mid-sentence into descriptions of harmonic intervals; correspondence continues in three parallel arguments

exits.label: back down to the still mirror
the tributary climbing toward its source, where copper was first mined
toward the settlement where the water was tested
downstream, where the taint becomes diluted into river
